subject: SEV1: tail latency + error spike on hosted API for long prompts
body:
From: Samir Patel <samir@cloudfin.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudFin Ops <ops+prod@cloudfin.ai>, Amanda Lee <amanda@cloudfin.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: [SEV1] p95/p99 spike on hosted API during long-context requests (16k window)

Sergio,

We're seeing a sustained p95/p99 regression and a sharp uptick in 5xx errors starting ~07:40 PT this morning for requests that use long contexts (most of our batch jobs are 16k tokens). Latency p99 jumped from ~1.8s to ~6.2s and error rate to ~3.5%. This is causing timeouts in our downstream processing.

We've attached a short trace and sampling of failing requests. Our traffic is steady; we didn't change payloads. Can you please investigate and advise ETA for mitigation? This is impacting batch reconciliation jobs and one of our nightly exports failed.

- Samir
CloudFin (Platform)

---

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cloudfin.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:24:15 -0700
Subject: Re: [SEV1] p95/p99 spike on hosted API during long-context requests (16k window)

Samir — thanks for the report and trace. I’m escalating to eng and CS. We’ll triage immediately and come back within 30 minutes with next steps.

Short-term asks from our side: can you confirm whether those requests include function calls or tool integrations? Also send a sample request id if you can (we already have the traces, but request ids help correlate).

— Sergio
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:51:02 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SEV1 - initial triage notes

FYI — quick triage from runtime: initial signal looks correlated with requests >8k tokens and magnifies at 16k/32k. Early hypothesis: KV-prefetch pattern combined with large attention state is causing outlier batch formation and de-scheduled worker stalls under our current batching window.

What we saw in the sampled traces:
- Repeated spike in queue_time and worker_deschedule metrics immediately before token-generation spikes.
- Several requests show KV cache miss churn and subsequent synchronous fetch cycles (trace id: trace-7c3b-20j).
- P95 increased across the fleet where long-context traffic is concentrated (west-us).

Attachments: trace-20260720-CloudFin.txt (stripped trace), kv-cache-heatmap-20260720.png

Action items I’m assigning:
1) Hiro: reproduce locally with 16k/32k synthetic prompts (I will share repro plan).
2) Marcus: check autoscaler logs for any transient pod restarts or scheduling events in the west-us cluster.
3) Neha: surface impacted customers list and recommend temporary credits.

I’ll post updates as we get reproduction.

— Evelyn
Principal SRE, Runtime Performance

---

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:03:40 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: SEV1 - initial triage notes

On Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 08:51 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> FYI — quick triage from runtime: initial signal looks correlated with requests >8k tokens and magnifies at 16k/32k. Early hypothesis: KV-prefetch pattern combined with large attention state is causing outlier batch formation and de-scheduled worker stalls under our current batching window.

Repro status: I reproduced a p99 tail locally using the repro-plan-16k-32k.md. Key findings:
- When a single request includes ~16k tokens plus long response generation (2-3k tokens), the runtime constructs huge KV frames that occasionally exceed the fast-path memory pool and trigger a synchronous fallback memory path. That fallback introduces a ~250-450ms stall per request, which accumulates when combined with existing queueing.
- Batch controller is grouping long requests together due to identical route and no per-request token limit; combined effective batch size spikes and serialization time rises superlinearly.
- Observed one production worker that hit a GC pause while handling a 32k window request; the autoscaler did not evict the worker in time.

Proposed immediate mitigations (to deploy in next 2-3 hours if approved):
A) Emergency config: enforce soft per-request context cap at 20k tokens for hosted API (reject or redirect to dedicated/private).
B) Enable model-fallback for long-context: route long requests to a memory-optimized model variant with staged KV streaming (reduces synchronous fallbacks).
C) Quick patch to batch controller to prefer mixing short and long requests (reduces coalesced long-only batches).

I’ll attach the detailed repro traces and the CPU/memory snap that show the fallback events.

— Hiro
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

---

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Executive Leadership <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 12:14:08 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary + customer ask: CloudFin hosted API tail latency (SEV1)

Team — heads up: CloudFin (strategic enterprise account) reported a SEV1 impacting batch processing. Engineering repro shows long-context requests (16k/32k) trigger synchronous KV fallbacks and batch coalescing that produce a p99 spike and increased 5xxs. Currently affecting west-us hosted clusters and a small set of customers.

Proposed immediate plan (seeking approval to proceed now):
- Approve temporary soft cap at 20k tokens for hosted API and automatic routing of >20k requests to Dedicated/Private variants or return a structured error with migration guide.
- Push the batch-controller quick patch (low-risk, feature-flagged) to reduce long-only batch coalescing; rollback safe.
- Notify impacted customers (Laura will lead comms) and offer one week service credit for CloudFin while we stabilize.

Why we need exec sign-off: customer credits and any change to routing/pricing needs approval from Revenue Ops if it affects invoicing, plus we want go/no-go for making the soft cap global vs region-scoped.

Sergio (CS) recommends immediate approval for region-scoped soft cap in west-us only, while engineering prepares a more nuanced rollout.

— Sergio
Head of Customer Success

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cloudfin.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Lee <amanda@cloudfin.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:02:25 -07:00
Subject: Re: SEV1 - hosted API long-context impact & next steps

Samir — thanks for the quick report and for attaching traces. We’ll communicate the mitigation plan and ETA.

Immediate actions we will take:
- Short-term: we will apply a west-us scoped soft cap (20k tokens) to reduce tail incidents and start routing >20k to a memory-optimized variant in ~2 hours. This should reduce p99 and 5xx incidents.
- CS will schedule a 30-min post-mortem with your platform team tomorrow to review migration options for large batch jobs.
- We will credit CloudFin one week of hosted API usage while we stabilize — I’ll follow up with billing on the exact figure.

Next update: I’ll post in ~90 minutes after engineering attempts the quick patch.

— Laura
Director, Customer Success Operations

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:04:30 -07:00
Subject: RE: Postmortem plan and follow-ups (CloudFin SEV1)

Quick closure note: batch-controller patch deployed to west-us in a canary (10% traffic) at 14:30 PT on 2026-07-21. Early indicators: p99 tail reduced ~45% for long-context synthetic traffic; no visible increase in overall error rate.

Next tasks:
- Hiro to validate full fleet rollout plan and stress test with 32k windows tonight.
- Neha to finalize customer credit amount and send invoice adjustments.
- Sergio/Laura to run the postmortem with CloudFin on Wed 07/22.

Attachments: repro-plan-16k-32k.md

— Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Runtime
